name: WENO5-M (mapped Jiang-Shu weights), finite-difference flux form
source: Henrick, Aslam and Powers, J. Comput. Phys. 207 (2005) 542-567: the mapping g_k(w) = w (d_k + d_k^2 - 3 d_k w + w^2) / (d_k^2 + w (1 - 2 d_k)), eq. (43) p. 555, applied to the normalised Jiang-Shu weights (eq. (44)) and renormalised (eqs. (46)-(47)); fifth order at f' = 0 'even near critical points where f' = 0' (p. 557, eps = 1e-40 in the numerics, Table 4); for r = 3 the rate at n_cp = 2 is 2 for the JS and the mapped weights alike, r_c = max(2r - 2 - n_cp, n_cp), eq. (60) p. 565 and Table 10 p. 566, derived with eps = 0. Every order there is for the derivative approximation (the flux difference)

claims.why: JS weights d_k + O(dx^2); g_k(d_k) = d_k, g_k'(d_k) = g_k''(d_k) = 0 (Henrick et al. eq. (45)), so the mapped weights are d_k + O(dx^6)
the linear part has a non-zero dx^5 term
Henrick et al. p. 557 and Table 10: fifth order at n_cp = 1. JS weights d_k + O(dx) at both stencils (their eq. (39)), mapped to d_k + O(dx^3): O(dx^3) dx^3 / dx = O(dx^5)
the linear part has a non-zero dx^5 term at f' = 0
eps comparable to beta_k = O(dx^4): the JS weights are still d_k + O(dx) (as with eps = 0, scaled by beta/(eps + beta)), and the map makes that O(dx^3)
mapped weight errors O(dx^3) times candidate errors O(dx^3)
eps fixed: JS weights d_k + O(dx^2), mapped O(dx^6)
Henrick et al. eq. (60), Table 10: rate 2 at n_cp = 2; convex weights of third-order candidates give O(dx^3)/dx in any case

Henrick et al. eq. (60), Table 10: r_c = max(2r - 2 - n_cp, n_cp) = 2 for r = 3, n_cp = 2, mapped or not: the leading JS weights are not d_k ((121/108, 1/36, 121/108) f'''^2 dx^6 indicators), and the map moves only weights near d_k

the limit JS weights are about (0.0001, 0.9996, 0.0003); g_k maps them to about (0.001, 1, 0.001), so the mapped weights tend to about (0, 1, 0), and sum_k (omega_k - d_k) A_k with A = (1/4, -1/12, 1/12) f''' is about -0.08 f''' != 0 at dx^3. The exact limit is not computed
